titulo: Git: the safety net for undoing any change
lead: In a single task, the agent can change ten files at once. Without a history, you don't know what changed or how to go back. With Git, every good version is kept with a date and an explanation, and a change you didn't approve goes back with one command.
objetivo: save versions with status, add, diff and commit, and undo an agent's change with git restore, without panic.
hero_alt: Sheets of paper pinned in a row on a clothesline against a dark wall, next to a notebook computer.

aprende.t: Start the history only in the project folder
Read git status and git diff before saving
Save a version with a message that says what changed
Bring a file back with git restore and undo a version with git revert

secoes.sub: The three stages of a file in Git. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: The agent created or changed files. git status shows each one: "Untracked files" are the ones Git isn't tracking yet; "Changes not staged" are changes that haven't been set aside yet.
git add with the file name sets aside only that file for the next version (Git calls this staging). git diff --cached shows, line by line, what will go in.
The commit staples together what you set aside. The message is the photo's caption: a verb and an object, like "Adds contact section". "update" says nothing a month from now.

Change not saved yet: git restore returns the file to the last saved version (and discards what changed). Version already saved: git revert creates a new version that undoes the earlier one, without erasing the history.

secoes.volta: Golden rule: commit before asking for a big change
secoes.legenda: Git runs only on your computer, with no internet. GitHub is another step, optional (lesson 8).

rolagem_fim.texto: Commit before you ask. The agent makes the change. You look with status and diff. Like it: add and commit. Don't like it: restore. Every good version becomes a point you can go back to.

secoes.titulo: From git init to your first undo

texto: Inside meu-primeiro-agente, git init creates the history. Never in your whole personal folder.
git config user.name and user.email, without --global, say who is saving, only in this project. The email appears in every version and is visible if the folder is published.
git status tells you which step each file is at. Always run it before setting anything aside.
This is where the .gitignore from lesson 5 proves itself: the .env doesn't show up in the list.
To learn, name the files in git add. The shortcut git add . sets aside everything that isn't ignored, including the personal note forgotten in the folder.
git log --oneline shows the short list of versions, one per line.

exemplo.texto: Creates README, AGENTS.md and a list of what not to keep

passos.sub: Find out where the change is
texto: Only in the file, not saved: git restore file. In a saved version: git revert with the version's code, which shows up in the log.
Check the open file, not just the terminal's reply.

exemplo.texto: The revert fixes it and leaves all three versions in the history.

secoes.sub: In the meu-primeiro-agente folder. Replace whatever is between < >.

blocos.rot: cmd · start and say who you are (only in this folder)
blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente
git init
git config user.name "<Your Name>"
git config user.email "<your@email.com>"
git status

blocos.rot: cmd · look, set aside and save the first version
blocos.conteudo:
git add README.md AGENTS.md .gitignore .env.example index.html
git diff --cached
git commit -m "primeira versão"
git log --oneline

blocos.rot: cmd · after the agent changed something
cmd · didn't like it: put the file back
cmd · like it? Save the new version
blocos.conteudo:
git add index.html
git commit -m "<o que mudou, com verbo>"

blocos.rot: cmd · undo a version you already saved
blocos.conteudo:
git log --oneline
git revert <código da versão>

abas.html:
On branch master
No commits yet
Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
        .env.example
        .gitignore
        AGENTS.md
        README.md
        index.html

"Untracked files" = outside the history. The .env isn't in the list: the .gitignore worked.

• Untracked files: files Git isn't tracking yet.
  • Changes to be committed: set aside, they go into the next version.
  • Changes not staged: changed, but not set aside.
  • nothing to commit, working tree clean: nothing has changed since the last version.

• git init in your home folder: Git starts watching Documents, Downloads, everything. Run cd first and check the path.
  • Skipping Git: the agent's first bad change turns into manual rework.
  • "Please tell me who you are": the git config for name and email is missing.

secoes.titulo: Rehearse: save, break it, and go back
secoes.sub: The agent is going to change index.html along the way.

missoes.pede: Start the history in this folder.
missoes.explica: The history lives in the hidden .git folder, just for this project.

missoes.pede: Check the state of the files.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
No commits yet
Untracked files:
        .env.example
        .gitignore
        AGENTS.md
        README.md
        index.html
missoes.explica: Five files outside the history, and no .env. That's the proof from lesson 5. (master or main is just the name of the main line; in lesson 8 it becomes main.)

missoes.pede: Set aside everything that isn't ignored.
missoes.explica: Now you can use the shortcut: you just checked in the status that there's nothing personal in the list.

missoes.pede: Save the first version with the message primeira versão.
missoes.explica: Version saved, with a short code (5f6c1eb). The numbers are examples.

missoes.pede: The agent rewrote the page and you didn't like it. Check the state.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
Changes not staged for commit:
        modified:   index.html
missoes.explica: "modified": index.html changed since the last version and hasn't been saved yet.

missoes.pede: Take index.html back to the last saved version.
missoes.explica: Silence is success. The agent's change was discarded.

missoes.pede: Check that everything is back to how it was.
missoes.saida:
On branch master
nothing to commit, working tree clean
missoes.explica: "working tree clean": the folder matches the saved version. Undone with one command, no panic.

secoes.fim: Full cycle: save, see the change, and go back. Do the same in your project.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: the codes and counts in the responses are examples.

secoes.sub: In the meu-primeiro-agente folder, with the agent open in another cmd window.

exercicios.texto: git init, config, status, add and commit. Ask the agent for a big change to the page and, if you don't like it, go back with git restore.
exercicios.pronto: you undid an agent change with one command, and git status says "working tree clean".

exercicios.texto: Ask for two small changes and save each one with a message that says what changed. Then undo the last one with git revert.
exercicios.pronto: git log --oneline shows the versions with clear messages, including the revert one, and the page went back to what it was.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The agent made a big change you didn't approve, and you haven't saved anything since. What should you do?
opcoes: git restore on the file, going back to the last saved version.
Delete the folder and start over.
Ask the agent to remember how it was.
perguntas.explica: With a commit before the change, git restore brings the file back in one command. That's why: commit before asking for a big change.

perguntas.p: Why name the files in git add instead of always using git add .?
opcoes: So you don't bring along a file you didn't want in the history.
Because the dot doesn't work on Windows.
perguntas.explica: The dot stages everything that isn't ignored, including a forgotten personal note. Use the shortcut only after checking the status.

perguntas.p: Which of these commit messages will help you a month from now?
opcoes: Adds a contact section to index.html
perguntas.explica: Verb and object: the list of versions already tells you what changed, without opening a file.

perguntas.p: A version that was already saved was wrong. Which command undoes it without erasing the history?
perguntas.explica: Revert is the newspaper's correction notice: it creates a new version that undoes the previous one. Restore is for a change that hasn't been saved yet.
